newsitem.title: USA: Conn. judge rejects accused rapist's bond request.
newsitem.headline: Conn. judge rejects accused rapist's bond request.

text.p: A Connecticut judge on Friday rejected a request by accused rapist Alex Kelly for more liberal bond so that he can leave his home unescorted.
Kelly, 29, is charged with raping two teenage girls in 1986. He fled to Europe to escape prosecution and remained in hiding for eight years.
The alleged rapes are being tried separately. His first trial ended with a deadlocked jury and his second trial was slated to start next April. No date has been set yet for the second case.

Kelly appeared in court Friday with his parents, asking to be allowed outside during the day without their supervision. He is free on $1 million bond and is not allowed outside his home after 6 p.m. Kelly has said he wants to attend classes at Norwalk Community Technical College, attend a gym in Stamford and perform volunteer work at an inner-city organisation.
In rejecting the request, Stamford Superior Court Judge Martin Nigro said, "It was not what I had in mind. I need some assurance that the defendant will be under supervision."
Prosecutor Bruce Hudock told the court: "These conditions were imposed to save him from himself and the community from potential harm."
Hudock called Kelly's bond request "a ludicrous schedule presented to the court because (Kelly) is homebound and can't take it any more."

Kelly's defence lawyer said he would file another bond motion next week to clarify Kelly's request. Kelly was due back in court on Jan. 15. Nigro said he would hear further arguments on the motion to modify the bond when they were filed.
